questions.text: A system administrator issues the apt-get upgrade command on a Linux operating system. What is the purpose of this command?
options: Every application installed will update itself to the latest version.
Operating system updates are downloaded and will be installed.
The remote repository of applications and dependencies will be updated to the latest version.
A specific application named upgrade will be installed.
questions.explanation: apt-get upgrade installs newer versions of the packages already on the system. The third option describes apt-get update, which only refreshes the local list of what the repositories have available and installs nothing — the two are almost always run in that order, update then upgrade.

questions.text: A Linux system administrator is searching the passwd file for any username that starts with a digit. Which grep command should the administrator use?
questions.explanation: ^ anchors the match to the start of the line and [0-9] matches a single digit, so '^[0-9]' finds lines beginning with a digit. Without the anchor, '[0-9]' matches a digit anywhere on the line — which would return nearly every line, since each one carries a UID and a GID.

questions.text: What is the output when the following code is entered into a Python interpreter?
questions.explanation: + concatenates two lists: the second is appended to the end of the first, in order. Nothing is sorted — the first option is what you would get from sorted([1,2,4,5] + [3,6]).

questions.text: What is displayed after the following code is entered into a Python interpreter?
options: nothing (because the print command is wrong)
a syntax error, because there should not be a space between the numerical values
questions.explanation: 22 + 10 is evaluated and bound to addition, then print() displays 32. Whitespace around an operator makes no difference to Python's parser.

questions.text: A Linux administrator is attempting to use a terminal to configure the network interface card on a computer. The administrator receives a message that they do not have the necessary permissions to perform the configuration. What should be done prior to the configuration command?
options: change the chmod permissions on the network configuration file
questions.explanation: Configuring an interface changes system state, so it needs root. sudo runs that one command as root, prompting for your own password, and drops straight back to your normal shell. Loosening the permissions on the config file instead would be working around the protection rather than using it.

questions.text: A network engineer needs to review the status of all network interfaces of a server running a Linux operating system. The engineer enters the command ifconfig -a. What is the result of this command?
options: All active interfaces will display information.
The ARP table of the computer will be displayed.
Both active and inactive interfaces will display information.
The host routing table will be displayed.
questions.explanation: -a means all: without it, ifconfig lists only the interfaces that are up. Worth knowing that ifconfig is deprecated on current distributions — the DEVASC VM's own labs use ip address for this, and ip route for the routing table.

questions.text: A system administrator attempts to determine what is causing a computer to perform slower than normal. The administrator issues the ps command. What is displayed by this command?
questions.explanation: ps reports the running processes and the CPU time each has used. Memory and disk are not its job — free reports RAM and df reports disk space.

questions.text: A user issues the Linux command ls -l myfile.sh to check the permissions of the file myfile.sh. Which two statements describe the permissions assigned to the file? (Choose two.)
questions.context:
devasc@labvm:~/Documents$ ls -l myfile.sh
-rwxr-xr-- 1 self test 15 Mar 30 21:24 myfile.sh
options: Any user in the self group can read, modify, and execute the file.
The user with the user ID of self can modify the file.
The user with the user ID of devasc can modify the file.
All users can execute the file.
Any user in the test group can execute the file.
questions.explanation: Read the string in three blocks after the leading type dash: owner rwx, group r-x, others r--. The owner is self and the group is test. So self has write and can modify it, and anyone in test has execute. The traps: self is the owning user, not a group; devasc is only the account at the prompt, and falls under others with r--; and others have no x, so not all users can execute it.

questions.text: Which Python command creates a conditional control structure?
questions.explanation: if, with elif and else, is Python's conditional. def defines a function and from imports from a module; delay is not a Python keyword at all. Repetition uses for and while.

questions.text: A user enters the commands as shown. What is the result after the mv command is entered?
options: The file myfile.sh is copied to the /home/devasc/Desktop directory and renamed as myfile2.sh.
The file myfile.sh is copied to the /home/devasc/Desktop directory and replaces the file myfile2.sh.
The file myfile.sh is copied and renamed to myfile2.sh in the current directory.
The file myfile.sh is moved to the /home/devasc/Desktop directory and renamed as myfile2.sh.
questions.explanation: mv moves rather than copies, so nothing is left behind in Documents — that rules out the three options that say copied. Because the destination path ends in a different filename, the file is renamed as part of the same move.

questions.text: A student new to Python is working in interactive interpreter mode and issues the command shown. Which data type is used to represent the variable ipAddress?
questions.explanation: Curly braces holding key:value pairs make a dictionary. Square brackets would have made a list and parentheses a tuple; Python has no built-in type called array.

questions.text: Working with the same dictionary, which Python expression retrieves the IP address of R2?
questions.explanation: A dictionary value is looked up by its key in square brackets. The key is the string "R2", so it needs its quotes — ipAddress[R2] would look for a variable named R2 and raise a NameError. Curly braces only build the dictionary; they never index it.

questions.text: A user issues a series of Linux commands as shown. Which directory is the current directory after the cd command is entered?
questions.explanation: .. is the parent directory, so ../.. goes up two levels in one step: backups to ansible, then ansible to labs.

questions.explanation: Concatenation first gives ['RT1', 'RT2', 'SW1', 'SW2', 'RT3', 'SW3']. Indexing starts at zero, so del hostnames[3] removes the fourth item, 'SW2' — not 'SW1', which is the trap.

questions.text: A student is learning Python in interactive interpreter mode and issues the commands shown. What is the result of the last line?
options: TypeError: a string type cannot be multiplied by an integer
questions.explanation: Multiplying a string by an integer repeats it that many times. y is 2, so 'Test' * y is 'TestTest'. The y*3 on the line before is ordinary arithmetic and does not change y — it is still 2, which is why the answer is not six copies.

questions.text: A student is reviewing the Python script shown. Under which condition will the elif statement be evaluated?
questions.context:
aclNum = int(input("What is the IPv4 ACL number? "))
if aclNum >= 1 and aclNum <= 99:
     print("This is a standard IPv4 ACL.")
elif aclNum >=100 and aclNum <= 199:
     print("This is an extended IPv4 ACL.")
else:
     print("This is not a standard or extended IPv4 ACL.")
options: when the input is a float number
when the first print statement fails
when the input is a string
when the if statement is false
questions.explanation: A chain is tested top to bottom and stops at the first branch that is true: elif is only reached once the if above it evaluates false. If the if is true, its block runs and the rest of the chain is skipped entirely. A string typed at the prompt would not reach the chain at all — int() would raise a ValueError first.

questions.explanation: Each entry carries permissions, link count, owner, group, size and date, which is exactly what -l adds.
